meta.parties: Babunona Et Al. v. Cornelis Appu

rules.statement: A partition decree is conclusive against all persons, and the only remedy for a party aggrieved by it is an action for damages.
rules.supporting_quote: "And a proviso to the section safeguards the right of any party prejudiced by a partition to recover damages from the parties who have caused him the prejudice, it has been held by the Supreme Court in numerous cases, of which it will suffice to refer to Nonohamy v. De Silva, 1 [(1891) 9 S. C. C. 198.] that under section 9 of Ordinance No. 10 of 1863 the partition decree is conclusive against the whole world, and that the only remedy open to a party aggrieved by it is the action of damages preserved by the proviso."
